evidence.text: 3Q26 fuel ran well above the $3.20/gal all-in assumption in the guide. Delta's 3Q (reported 2026-10-09) realised $3.61 against a $3.15 July assumption, +46c or about +15%, and absorbed more than $500m of fuel above guidance. On about 118m gallons (2Q used 444.7m litres = ~117.5m gal), the same overrun costs Aeromexico roughly $50-70m, or 3-4.5 points of margin on $1.6bn of revenue. That puts the 14-17% operating-margin and 26.5-29.5% EBITDAR guide at risk unless pricing recaptures more than 2Q's ~75%. The overrun in 2Q was only $30m, and 2Q still landed in line with guidance.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last confirmed print, 2Q26 (2026-07-13 amc): results in line with guide despite a $30m fuel overrun and a net loss; the baseline records +2.29% for that session. The 1Q26 print (2026-04-21 amc) is not in the baseline history, whose other rows are monthly traffic reports, so there is no clean earnings base rate.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the CEO warned in the Aug and Sep traffic releases that fuel is 'higher than previously anticipated'. But no quantified Aeromexico number exists, the EPS estimates are scattered from $0.24 to $0.61, and targets sit at $27-28, so the size of the margin shortfall has not been set. If the market had fully priced a 3-4 point margin miss, the stock would not have risen about 6% since Delta's 10-09 print.
evidence.independence: Same direction from the company's own wording, in two separate releases: Sep traffic, 2026-10-06 (https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results), and Aug traffic, 2026-09-03 (https://www.itiger.com/news/2664877196). Guide assumption from the 2Q26 6-K. Shares the Delta document with the guidance finding below, but lands on a different line (the reported quarter vs the forward guide).

evidence.text: The 4Q26 and FY26 guide is built on $3.00/gal fuel, while Delta's 4Q guide (2026-10-09) assumes about $4.25. A gap of $1.00-1.25/gal on about 120m gallons is $120-150m, or 7-9 points of 4Q margin before recapture. So the 15.5-18.5% 4Q operating-margin guide and the 11-13% FY guide are very likely cut, or recast with a fare and capacity response. Precedent: Delta cut FY EPS by 24% at the midpoint and traded about -2.9%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No confirmed Aeromexico guidance cut since the Nov-2025 IPO. Peer precedent: Delta -2.9% on a 24% FY EPS cut whose midpoint ($5.35) was already near the $5.46 consensus (https://finviz.com/news/400853/delta-air-lines-shares-fall-as-third-quarter-earnings-miss-forecasts-and-full-year-outlook-is-cut).
evidence.why_not_priced: The stale $3.00 assumption sits in the company's own 6-K and has not been withdrawn. Aggregator targets ($27-28) and the spread in estimates suggest many models still carry the July guide. Had a 7-9 point 4Q margin reset been priced, AERO would not have rallied after Delta cut. The opposite case is also live: the cut is so widely expected that 'less bad' fare recapture could be bought.
evidence.independence: Delta's 4Q fuel assumption of $4.25 (https://beancount.io/blog/2026/10/10/delta-air-lines-q3-2026-earnings-analysis). The Aeromexico CEO's 2026-10-06 wording on fuel 'more challenging than anticipated' (https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results). Also, at the 2Q call (July) the company said it would cut 4Q capacity if fuel volatility persisted (https://www.elimparcial.com/dinero/2026/07/27/las-aerolineas-mexicanas-pierden-mas-de-3-mil-300-millones-de-pesos-por-el-fuerte-aumento-en-el-precio-de-la-turbosina-durante-el-segundo-trimestre-de-2026/).

evidence.text: 3Q traffic ran ahead of the capacity guide. Total RPMs were +2.9% y/y in August and +3.6% in September, against 3Q ASM guidance of +0.5% to +1.5%. Load factor was 89.7% in Aug (+0.6pp) and 87.1% in Sep (+0.1pp), and international RPMs grew +4.3% and +6.6%. Together with management's 'forward bookings healthy' wording, this points to revenue at or slightly above the $1.59-1.62bn guide.

evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the traffic releases are public. Yield (TRASM) is not in them, so the size of any revenue beat from fare recapture is the unpublished part.
evidence.independence: August traffic release, 2026-09-03 (https://www.itiger.com/news/2664877196). Delta reported record revenue +16% and said demand was strong (https://finviz.com/news/400853/delta-air-lines-shares-fall-as-third-quarter-earnings-miss-forecasts-and-full-year-outlook-is-cut).

evidence.text: Citi (as reported 2026-10-12) says Aeromexico is better placed than Volaris to pass high fuel through to fares, citing premium mix, long-haul international and its AICM hub, and expects no material demand damage. It also flags that AICM's move to 48 operations an hour at the end of October could restore slots. Citi calls a Volaris guidance revision 'probable' but makes no such call on Aeromexico.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a sell-side view and probably part of why AERO rose after Delta's cut, so it is largely in the price. It is filed because the call can confirm or deny the fare pass-through and the AICM slot gain.

evidence.independence: Bloomberg Law, 2026-08-20 (https://news.bgov.com/antitrust/delta-wins-challenge-of-dot-order-to-end-aeromexico-partnership).

evidence.text: Rates have moved past what Ally's guide assumed. On the Q2 call (2026-07-21) management said its forward curve as of June 30 assumed one hike in September 2026 and another in early 2027. Since then the Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16, the 10-year reached about 5.2% on 2026-09-25 (highest since 2007), and as of 2026-10-19 the market prices a December 2026 hike at about 75%, pulling the second hike forward. The 10-Q describes Ally's balance sheet as structurally liability-sensitive. That puts the 'exit above 3.7%' NIM language, which the stock trades on, at risk of being softened or pushed out on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM guidance is the line that moves this stock. The July 2026 print missed EPS by 1-2 cents with a reiterated NIM guide and fell 2.39%, then drifted down about 16%. The Barclays conference of 2026-09-15 guided Q3 NIM flat (rather than rising) and the shares fell about 3% that day (Goldesel). The baseline's largest reaction, +8.1% on 2026-04-17, came on a strong NIM print.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the stock is down about 16-17% since the print and fell about 11% in September as yields rose, and the skew pays for downside. What is not yet visible is whether management keeps or cuts the exit-NIM language. A cut is the remaining step, and the stock's position 4% above its 52-week low implies it is partly expected. Rates also eased in October (10-year about 5.06-5.13%, an October hold now priced at 83%), so the extreme scenario has faded.
evidence.independence: Rates data from Trading Economics (2026-09-25 item and stream through 2026-10-19): https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield/news/586974 . Liability sensitivity from the 10-Q of June 30, 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040729/000004072926000017/ally-20260630.htm . Cox Automotive (2026-10-07) also cites 'interest rates climbing rapidly'. This is macro-to-company transmission that the company itself has not confirmed.

evidence.text: Ally's deposit repricing after the September hike was small and late. Its high-yield savings APY went from 3.00% (unchanged on 2026-09-22, CDs raised that day) to 3.10% by about 2026-09-30, and was still 3.10% on 2026-10-13. That is about a 40% beta on a 25bp hike, applied only in the last week of Q3. Q2 average retail deposit yield was 3.12%, so Q3 deposit cost is likely flat. This supports the flat Q3 NIM guide and slows how fast the hike hits Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ally reported in Q2 that lower deposit costs drove NIM up 11bp quarter on quarter (2Q26 8-K). The baseline's largest positive reaction, +8.1% in April 2026, was on margin.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market sold the stock as yields rose, which treats it as fully rate-exposed. If low deposit beta were priced, the September drawdown would have been smaller than the move in yields implies. These are consumer rate-tracking pages, not what analysts read.
evidence.independence: DepositAccounts forum, 2026-09-22 (savings 3.00%, no change; CDs raised): https://www.depositaccounts.com/community/promos/63503-ally-rate-changes-9222026.html . evidence.text: Used-vehicle values weakened in September. The Manheim index was 205.9, down 1.1% from August and 0.6% from a year earlier (unadjusted: -1.3% month on month, -1.2% year on year), with 'steeper-than-normal September depreciation'. Cox cut its year-end 2026 forecast from +2% to +0.2%. Ally's Q2 net lease depreciation was already $269M against $216M a year earlier. Lower values pressure lease remarketing gains and auto loss severity heading into the seasonally worst Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit and NCO commentary was a driver at the September 2024 Barclays conference (cited in TheFly headline) and in Q3 2025, when retail auto NCO was 1.88% (down 36bp year on year) and the stock rose 3.56%.

evidence.text: Capital One's auto net charge-off rate was 1.66% in August 2026 (30+ day delinquency 4.54%), against 1.54% for its Q3 2025 quarter. Ally's Q3 2025 retail auto NCO was 1.88%, so a Q3 2026 rate at or above that would break its streak of year-on-year improvement.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Year-on-year NCO improvement was a selling point in the Q2 2026 call and the Q3 2025 beat (+3.56%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Capital One's monthly 8-Ks are watched, but the read-across to Ally's retail auto book is indirect. The comparison is a single month against a quarter, so it is noisy. Ally's own FY guide of 1.8-2.0% already allows for second-half normalization.
